# AI coding research brief — September 25, 2026

Historical backfill published October 17, 2026. Reconstructed from recovered prior-conversation findings; this is not a verbatim transcript. The original selections, reported results, caveats, and proposed experiments are preserved in condensed form. Dates below are publication dates recorded in the original brief. These are research proposals, not demonstrated Quadratus improvements or implementation instructions.

## 1. Who Holds the Pen? Let Specifications, Not Agents, Sign Off
**September 24, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29921v1)**

SpecHarness compiles visible specifications into source-linked obligations and allows qualified external evidence to establish completion. Across seven models and 87 SkillsBench tasks, macro verifier pass rate rose from 61.1% to 73.1%, while the completion-claim/verified-success gap fell from 32.8 to 12.8 percentage points.

**Why read it and limitations:** It separates a worker's assertion from evidence that the task is complete. Token use increased about 53%; guarantees cover machine-groundable obligations rather than the complete natural-language request. The comparison includes validation, feedback and repair, so it does not isolate the effect of the authority boundary alone.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Maintain an immutable obligation ledger tied to the request. Only external evidence can mark obligations satisfied, and relevant file changes invalidate earlier evidence. Measure verified completion and false completion alongside token overhead.

## 2. Where Does Exactly-Once Live? Model, Harness, and Tool-Contract Effects on Duplicate Side Effects in LLM Agents
**September 24, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29095v1)**

In a deterministic service sandbox, frontier models duplicated effects in 56% of in-flight cases and 74% of double-delivery cases. Offering idempotency keys on every write reduced duplication from 28% to 4%. Read-back checks alone cannot guarantee exactly-once effects with unbounded late commits.

**Why read it and limitations:** Coordinator retries need tool-level contracts as well as good reasoning. The services are simulated, workflows are short to medium length, and shared setup deliberately reduces some harness differences. The observed 4% rate is not an exactly-once guarantee.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Where tools support them, attach stable idempotency keys to mutating operations and centrally persist keys and outcomes. Test lost acknowledgements, late commits and retry recovery without creating duplicate effects.

## 3. SkillApt: Learning When to Activate Agent Skills from Counterfactual Evidence
**September 22, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26863v1)**

SkillApt decides whether to load a retrieved skill using matched with-skill/without-skill outcomes. On its frozen SRA-Bench evaluation, observed accuracy stayed at 83.8%, activation dropped from 100% to 31.5%, and mean token use fell 74.3%.

**Why read it and limitations:** A relevant skill may still be unnecessary or harmful. Evidence is sparse, skill identities were not held out, and activation boundaries do not transfer consistently across models. Matching observed accuracy does not prove universal equivalence.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Log matched outcomes by skill, model and task state. Begin with an observational LOAD/ABSTAIN policy before allowing it to change execution; compare accuracy, tokens and failure types separately for each assistant.

## 4. How Does Adversarial Influence Scale in Multi-Agent Systems?
**September 24, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.30028v1)**

The earlier brief reported that, in groups of 2–21 agents, adoption of incorrect answers rose approximately linearly with the proportion of deceptive participants. Adding honest participants did not ensure robustness.

**Why read it and limitations:** More agreeing agents may amplify a bad conclusion. The experiments cover two deliberation protocols and academic questions, not collaborative coding; the causal mechanism was not established.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Preserve each worker's independent answer. Route executable disagreements to evidence-producing verification and track correct-to-incorrect answer changes after discussion.

**Source status:** Preserved from the earlier brief; the source could not be independently reopened during this backfill. Treat the reported results as awaiting source re-verification.

## 5. NeuroTestGen: Neuro-Symbolic Guided Test Generation with LLMs
**September 24, 2026 · [Paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.30178v1)**

The earlier brief described symbolic execution generating path constraints, an LLM constructing realistic tests, and an iterative compile/execute/repair loop. With Claude Sonnet 4.6, it reported 92.91% average line coverage, 88.89% branch coverage and a 96.88% executable-test rate on a Java benchmark.

**Why read it and limitations:** Concrete uncovered paths can guide a testing worker more effectively than an open-ended request for more tests. Limitations include path explosion, heap modeling, iterative cost and one Java benchmark. Coverage alone does not establish assertion quality.

**Proposed Quadratus experiment:** Give a test-generation worker uncovered branches and constraints, use a separate model for compilation repair, and require measured coverage evidence before accepting improvement.

**Source status:** Preserved from the earlier brief; the source could not be independently reopened during this backfill. Treat the reported results as awaiting source re-verification.

## The single most promising idea to try

Implement an obligation ledger first: map each requested outcome to an owner and admissible evidence, invalidate evidence when relevant artifacts change, and let the coordinator accept completion only after checking that ledger. Compare verified success, unsupported completion claims and total cost against the current process.
